title: The Day the Leftover Candy Unionized
skyStory: A skinny eleven percent moon is lounging in Sagittarius, still wearing last night's costume and refusing to admit Halloween is over. Mars keeps hinting that the plastic skeleton on the porch should come down. Saturn has quietly filed the jack-o'-lanterns under compost. Outside, the maples are dropping their last leaves in dramatic little swoons, like actors who were told the play closes Friday.

reading: November arrives with a gust that slams one door in the house for no reason. Treat it as a starting pistol. You have nine days left in this year of readings, and the cabin wants its woodpile stacked neatly before the final chapter.

Around 10:20 am you will be tempted to start a project the size of a barn. The [[Knight of Wands]] snorts into its gauntlet. One shelf, one drawer, one email folder. Finish it so thoroughly it sparkles. Then sit back and admire it for a full minute, which is longer than you think, and do not use the minute to plan the next one.
joel.mission: Pick the single smallest unfinished thing in your home and finish it before noon, then announce its completion to an empty room.
joel.omen: A pumpkin sitting on a step with a slightly smug face. It means a small job is waiting to be called done.
joel.elementWhy: the first November gust clears the deck

reading: The tide went out further than usual this morning, and the Wood Rat noticed before anyone else. Something small and shiny got left behind on the sand of your day. Maybe a forgotten idea, maybe a note from last week. Pick it up.

By mid-afternoon someone will ask you to explain a thing you know inside out. Your hands will start moving before your mouth does, and that is how everyone will know the story is going to be good. Life Path 11 hums along underneath like a radiator. Let one listener walk away a level higher than they arrived. That is your quiet November magic.
nancy.mission: Rescue one fun-sized leftover from Halloween and give it to someone as if it were a medal of honour.
nancy.omen: A wet leaf stuck flat to a window, shaped almost like a hand. Someone nearby is about to wave hello in a big way.

together.text: Each of you describe last night's best costume you saw, real or imagined, in exactly seven words. Swap them. The more ridiculous description wins custody of the skeleton for one imaginary week.

game.intro: November 1st, and the leftover candy has unionized. Negotiate fast: three picks, ten seconds each, no treats withheld.
